rejected.title: Comparing management between countries
card: Countries often face the same problem, such as waste or floods, but they may manage it in different ways.
Money affects what a country can build or buy. Technology affects the tools it can use, such as recycling plants or flood warning systems.
Laws set the rules, such as bans on dumping or limits on building on floodplains. Values shape what people think matters most, such as protecting nature or protecting jobs.
To compare two countries, look at the same problem and ask how money, technology, laws and values led to different responses.
rejected.remember: Same problem, different management: money, technology, laws and values shape the response.

a.q: Country X bans new homes on floodplains. Country Y has no such rule, so people build there. Which factor explains this difference?
opts: Laws, which set rules on where people can build
Money, which decides what a country can afford
Technology, which decides the tools a country has
Values, which shape what people think matters most
a.why: The difference is a rule about where homes can go, and rules come from laws. Money and technology affect what a country can build or use, but neither is a rule that limits building.
a.clue: Is the difference about a rule, a cost or a tool?

b.q: Country A has a lot of money and recycling technology, and Country B has little of either. Both have a rubbish problem. What is the most likely difference in how they manage waste?
opts: Country A builds recycling plants, while B relies on dumps
Country B builds recycling plants, while A relies on dumps
Country B recycles more because it has less money to spend
Both use the same methods because they share the problem
b.why: Money and technology let Country A build recycling plants, while Country B is likely to use cheaper methods such as dumps. The reversed option gets this backwards, and sharing a problem does not mean countries manage it the same way.
b.clue: Ask which country can afford to build recycling plants.

a.q: Two countries face river floods. One builds levees and runs a warning system, while the other relies on local volunteers. What best explains the difference?
opts: Differences in money, technology, laws or values
The floods are a different problem in each country
Only one country has people who care about floods
Floods can be managed in only one correct way
a.why: The problem is the same, so the difference comes from what each country can afford, which tools it has, its laws and what it values. Saying floods can be managed in only one way ignores these differences.
a.clue: The problem is the same, so look at the factors behind the response.

b.q: Country A has a lot of money and recycling technology, and Country B has little of either. Both have a rubbish problem. What is the most likely difference in how they manage waste?
opts: Country A can build recycling plants, while B may use dumps
Country B will recycle more because it has less money
Both must use identical methods to deal with waste
Country A has less rubbish so it needs no plan
b.why: Money and technology let Country A build recycling plants, while Country B may have to use cheaper methods such as dumps. Less money does not cause more recycling, and countries do not have to use the same methods.
b.clue: Ask what each country can afford to build.

a.best: Differences in money, technology, laws or values

b.best: Country A can build recycling plants, while B may use dumps

problems.detail: The right option is the longest and the only one hedged with 'can' and 'may'. The distractors use absolute words ('needs no plan', 'must use identical methods', 'will recycle more'), so a student could pick the answer from the wording alone.

Two distractors use 'only' ('only one correct way', 'Only one country has people who care'), where the card says countries 'may' manage problems differently. The absolute wording marks them as wrong, which makes the right option easier to spot without knowing the idea.
